title: Delta-prefill quant path planner and lazy unpack flow to reduce dequant overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: At high throughput, the runtime pays a significant dequantization and memory-copy tax when switching between INT8/FP8 kernels and decode-time mixed-precision paths. This shows up as increased p95 latency during prefill-heavy workloads (long contexts) and poor amortization of kernel setup cost for short decode bursts.

Goal: Implement a lightweight planner that routes requests to quantization-friendly kernel variants based on observed delta in sequence length and KV-cache hits, and introduce a "lazy unpack" flow that delays full dequant until a kernel absolutely requires FP32 activations. The planner should: (1) prefer INT8/FP8 fused kernels when safe, (2) opportunistically prefetch dequantized tiles for near-future tokens, (3) avoid full eagerly-unpacked KV copies during prefill when attention patterns indicate decode will dominate, and (4) expose knobs for canary and rollback.

Why this is unique: instead of wholesale always-dequant or always-lazy approaches, we use a delta-prefill heuristic plus a tiny per-request estimator to choose mixed-precision execution paths at runtime and reduce memory churn without sacrificing model quality or safety constraints.
acceptance_criteria: p50 token generation latency for long-context prefill workloads improves or remains equal compared to baseline (-5% or within 2%)
p95 latency for mixed prefill+decode workload decreases by at least 12% on optimized models when using planner+lazy-unpack
end-to-end token cost (GEMM time + memory copies) reduced by >=9% in our perf harness for bert-small-like models and >=6% for decoder-only 7B variants
no increase in model misprediction rate beyond statistical noise on our regression prompt suite (quality delta within ±0.5% BLEU/ROUGE or equivalent evals we use)
feature gated behind runtime flag with canary rollout and automatic fallback to current kernel planner
unit and integration tests added; CI perf job reproduces benchmark and fails on regressions
technical_design:
High-level components:
- Delta Prefill Estimator: lightweight estimate (byte-sized structure) computed from request metadata: current sequence delta, kv_cache_hit_ratio, requested max_tokens, and last-model-variant. Runs in the request router.
- Precision Path Arbiter: small state machine that maps estimator output to one of: INT8-fused, FP8-fused, mixed-prefill/FP32-decode, or conservative-FP32. Decisions are cached per connection for a short TTL.
- Lazy Unpack Flow: instead of immediate dequant->FP32 copy of KV caches during prefill, we store quantized tiles with a small per-tile metadata bitmask and only materialize on first kernel that needs FP32 activations. Materialization is async and uses prefetch hints for near-future tokens.
- Kernel Adapter API: a minimal shim that exposes whether a kernel accepts quantized tile formats and a callback for on-demand unpack. Kernels will implement a two-stage prepare() that returns fast-path or slow-path.

Data structures: all new fields are byte-aligned and constrained to per-request arena; no global allocations. Prefetch uses the same pinned buffers as existing KV cache to avoid extra copies.

Compatibility: planner checks model capability metadata (from model catalog) for supported fused kernels. For models without INT8/FP8 kernel support, we default to existing code path.

Observability: add tracing spans for "delta_estimate", "precision_choice", "lazy_unpack_trigger", and metrics for "unpack_latency", "unpack_hits/misses", and per-model path distribution.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
Tradeoffs:
- Complexity: adds per-request decision logic and per-tile metadata which increases runtime code surface.
- Memory: lazy unpack reduces eager copies but keeps quantized tiles longer in memory which may increase pressure on allocators in extreme cases.
- Numeric correctness: subtle FP32/FP16 mixing risks; we must validate that fused INT8/FP8 kernels provide equivalent numerics for our eval prompts.

Risks and mitigations:
- If estimator misroutes too often, we will see tail regressions. Mitigation: conservative default and short-lived cache entries; immediate fallback on latency regressions.
- Prefetch contention could create extra GPU work. Mitigation: cap prefetch concurrency and use adaptive backoff based on GPU utilization metrics.
- Edge cases with third-party models: force catalog opt-in for older model recipes.
plan: Spike (3 days): implement estimator prototype in the router, add microbench harness to measure dequant latency and per-tile unpack cost
Design PR (2 days): land Kernel Adapter API and model catalog flags for fused-kernel capability
Core impl (7 days): implement arbiter, lazy-unpack buffers, and integration with prefiller and decode scheduler
Perf tuning (4 days): tune prefetch concurrency, tile size thresholds, and estimator thresholds
QA and canary (3 days): run regression suite, internal canary on staging cluster, gate by runtime flag
Rollout (2 days): staged rollout to 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback checks
testing_plan: Unit tests for estimator boundaries and Kernel Adapter API, integration tests that compare baseline vs planner with randomized sequences, synthetic perf harness that exercises long context prefill and many short decode bursts, and regression suite against our eval prompts. Add CI perf job that runs nightly and refuses merges on >2% p95 regression for core benchmarks.
rollout_plan: Feature-gated behind RUNTIME_QUANT_PATH flag. Canary targets: internal-staging -> canary-rt-1 (5%) -> canary-rt-2 (25%) -> all. Monitor p50/p95, unpack_miss_rate, and GPU utilization. Auto-roll back on p95 increase >5% or unpack_miss_rate > 10% relative to baseline.
notes: Initial microbench shows a 14% reduction in unpack time for decoder-only 6B baseline when using lazy-unpack with prefetch=2 tiles. Need to validate across A100 and H100 kernels. Coordinate with infra for vGPU mem pressure testing. Discussed prefetch limits with kernel team; they suggested 2-4 tile window as a safe default.
